newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp declines comment on AmEx.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp declines comment on AmEx.

text.p: Citicorp executive vice president William Campbell declined comment on rumors that failed merger talks between Citicorp and American Express Co have been revived, when questioned Tuesday by analysts.
"I have no comment on American Express," said the executive, who heads Citicorp's consumer business.

Campbell did say Citicorp is looking for strategic alliances and joint ventures. He cited a program with Blockbuster stores in Colombia and Peru. He said that, in addition to retailers, telecommunications companies would be candidates for alliances.

Commenting on other types of acquisitions, Campbell said Citicorp was keeping an "open line" on whether to to make its own financial products or buy them in acquisitions. He said the company will look at opportunities for acquisitions but does not believe that one is essential.
Citicorp has been trying to build up its retirement products after getting a late start in the business. It recently hired a top executive from the Putnam mutual fund group.
Campbell said one corporate goal is to have one billion customers by the year 2010.
Also commenting on possible acquisitions was Thomas Jones, executive vice president and principal financial officer. He noted there have been a lot of deals "costing an arm and a leg these days."
He said Citicorp will continue to have a disciplined approach to acquisitions.
